headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER SCRAPS $45M SPROTT SILVER STREAM — DEBT GONE FOR EQUITY
snippet: Americas Gold & Silver (TSX:USA) agreed May 22 to hand Sprott Mining Inc. 7.96M shares at US$5.57 each, cancelling the remaining 592,000 oz silver delivery obligation and wiping out more than $45M in variable debt. The original stream was established as part of a Dec 2024 consolidation deal. Shares subject to a four-month TSX hold period.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER DRILLS 890 g/t AgEq OVER 51.5M AT BOUMADINE — ZONE OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver's infill drill program at the Boumadine project (Morocco) intersected 890 g/t silver-equivalent over 51.5m, including 1,504 g/t AgEq over 19.3m, confirming high-grade continuity. A new mineralized parallel structure was discovered 70m below the current resource pit shell. Over 69,000m drilled at Boumadine in 2026 to date.

headline: CORE LITHIUM RESTARTS FINNISS MINE AS SPODUMENE PRICES TRIPLE FROM 2024 SHUTDOWN LEVELS
snippet: Core Lithium restarted blasting and excavation at the Finniss spodumene operation (Northern Territory, Australia) after securing A$290M in financing. Spodumene concentrate has recovered to ~$4,200/t — roughly three times the price at which the mine was placed on care and maintenance in 2024 — with first exports targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: SILVER SURGES 2.4% TO $76.24, GOLD HOLDS $4,504 — RATIO COMPRESSES TO 59 AS PHYSICAL BUYERS STEP IN
snippet: Silver staged a sharp reversal on May 21, gaining 2.41% to $76.24/oz while gold held steady at $4,504/oz — still 20% below its January all-time high of $121.64. The gold/silver ratio compressed to 59:1, its tightest in several sessions, as physical buyers stepped in aggressively on the recent pullback. J.P. Morgan sees silver averaging $81/oz in 2026.

headline: AI EXPLORATION PLATFORM MinersAI EXPANDS INTO ASIA-PACIFIC, TARGETS ASX JUNIORS
snippet: MinersAI, an artificial intelligence platform that analyzes geological datasets and assists junior mining teams with drill targeting, has expanded its services to the Asia-Pacific region. The company is targeting ASX-listed explorers operating across Australia, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Rim who are increasingly adopting AI-driven workflows to reduce exploration spend.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $84.70/LB ON AI NUCLEAR DEMAND — UTILITIES SIT OUT, CAMECO PIPELINE AT RISK
snippet: Uranium edged to $84.70/lb on May 21, up 20% year-on-year, even as utilities stay sidelined by geopolitical uncertainty. Long-term demand is underpinned by AI data center nuclear deals — Meta has signed for up to 7.8 GW of nuclear capacity. Analysts warn Cameco and Kazatomprom face pipeline shortfalls into the 2030s without accelerated project development.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS HOLDS $5,400/OZ GOLD TARGET — EM CENTRAL BANKS BUYING 60 TONNES A MONTH
snippet: Goldman Sachs reaffirmed its $5,400/oz year-end gold forecast after the metal's 10%-plus March correction, citing ~60 tonnes/month of emerging-market central bank purchases, 500 tonnes of Western ETF inflows since early 2025, and rising concerns over US fiscal credibility as durable structural drivers. A geopolitical stress scenario extends the upside range to $5,700–$6,100.

headline: SOUTHERN COPPER COMMITS $319M TO 17-MONTH CUAJONE MINE OVERHAUL IN PERU
snippet: Southern Copper (NYSE:SCCO) will spend $318.6M over 17 months upgrading its Cuajone copper mine in Moquegua, Peru — including a new filter press at the concentrator — to lower costs and maintain concentrate quality during shutdowns. Cuajone produced ~163,000 tonnes of fine copper in 2025 within the company's overall 911,400-tonne 2026 guidance.

headline: COCHILCO RAISES 2026 COPPER PRICE FORECAST TO $5.55/LB — ENERGY TRANSITION DEMAND HOLDING FIRM
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco lifted its 2026 average price forecast to $5.55/lb and its 2027 outlook to $5.10/lb, citing sustained demand from EVs, grid infrastructure, and AI data centres. Copper hit a record $6.65/lb on May 13 before pulling back to around $6.28, with a 2026 market deficit of ~350,000 tonnes still projected.

headline: NdPr STILL 88% HIGHER YTD AFTER 21% APRIL DROP — TRUMP-XI SUMMIT SPOTLIGHTS RARE EARTH CHAINS
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since Q1's rally — yet remains 88% above January's $53/kg opening. The Trump-Xi summit in May elevated rare earth supply chains to a central bilateral issue. Critical Metals (CRML) broke ground on a Greenland pilot plant and signed a $1.5B JV term sheet with a Saudi conglomerate.

headline: COEUR MINING DECLARES INAUGURAL DIVIDEND AFTER NEW GOLD ACQUISITION — $0.02/SHARE SEMI-ANNUAL
snippet: Coeur Mining (NYSE:CDE) declared its first-ever dividend — $0.02/share semi-annually — payable June 10 to holders of record May 22, following its March 20 acquisition of New Gold Inc. The combined company now operates seven wholly-owned mines across North America in gold, silver, and copper, and set out a financial policy of semi-annual dividends going forward.

headline: CHINA IMPORTS 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — SOLAR SURGE LOCKS IN SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly SWOT analysis highlights China's record silver appetite — 790-plus tonnes imported in early 2026 — driven overwhelmingly by booming solar panel production. The Silver Institute projects a 67 million oz structural supply deficit in 2026, marking the sixth consecutive year that global silver demand has outpaced mine supply and recycling combined.
